svg.text: MPx Boil-Tube: heat a little, cool through the tubes (v0.4)
Gravity feeds water through a tube-in-tube coil into a 60 mL boil cell. A wax valve lets it out only when it is ~95 °C, and the same coil cools it on the way down. No pump, no PCB, no battery.
Ø104 × 420 mm · ~1.0 kg · 0.6 L reservoir · 0.8–1.6 L/h
Section, not to scale. Blue: cold feed up the outer tube. Red: boiled water down the inner tube.
B · One pass of water (1.2 L/h, 25 °C room)
the same coil: heat passes from the inner tube to the outer
Why it needs so little power: the coil hands ~95% of the heat from outgoing water to incoming water (ε 0.95). The heater only makes up the
last few degrees, steam and losses: ~22 W at 1.2 L/h, against ~121 W with no coil. The same tubes are the cooler: water leaves at ~27 °C
C · All the electrics: 7 parts, no PCB
Temperature control is mechanical: water can't pass the wax gate
until it is ~95 °C, so there is no sensor or controller. The heater
simply runs; spare power goes into steam, and the vent tube returns
Power: any 65 W+ USB-C charger, or a 100 W power bank off-grid. Per
litre ~19 Wh plus ~12 min of warm-up, so a 90 Wh bank gives about 3
Two dry-boil cut-offs (130 °C thermostat, 152 °C fuse) on the
thermowell. 20 V only: no mains inside. The cell is vented, so
D · Prototype now from stock parts
Boil cell: 1.5" SS316 tri-clamp spool 100 mm + 2 end caps
SS316 tube: 3/16" × 3.8 m and 3/8" × 2.4 m; coil by hand on
24 V 60 W cartridge heater + KSD301 130 °C + TCO + fuse +
24 V 3 A DC adapter for the bench (USB-C PD trigger for the
Wax gate: car-engine thermostat (~88–92 °C) in a 2"
tri-clamp housing; check its opening temp
1/8" SS needle valve at the spout
Reservoir: 1 L glass aspirator bottle with bottom outlet +
Body: finned Al heat-sink tube or radiator fin strip, coil
Aerogel wrap, 3D-printed frame, 2 bimetal thermometers for
≈ ₹15,000 bench prototype (full list in the BOM)
Big and modular is fine: every joint is a clamp or compression fitting,
so the coil length, cell size and gate can be swapped while testing.
E · Numbers (sims T1–T5) and fit to the requirements
Portable bottle form; tubes + body do the cooling as asked; 7 electrical
parts, no PCB/battery (req 9.3); runs from a power bank (req 4.1/4.6);
continuous flow, drinkable straight away (req 2.1); no plastic on the wet side
Removal needs hard water (~285 mg/L for 90%, req 10.1). ~22 parts (req 9.2 ≤
20). Product parts ~₹2,000 → retail ~₹6,600: above the ₹5,000 quartile, below
Wax-gate opening temperature and leakage; lime scaling the 3/16" inner tube
(needs a citric-acid flush); mesh clogging at the gate; air locks when

1) Gate: opening temperature and that nothing passes below it. 2) Coil ε and outlet temperature at 0.8/1.2/1.6 L/h with 4 thermometers. 3) Lime formed in 2–3 min in the 60 mL cell (titration). 4) Bead removal, Nile Red counts (Concept 05). 5) Scale
in the inner tube after 20 L.
